items.title: The miners' strike
items.line: The strike began with a walkout at Cortonwood Colliery on 6 March 1984 and ran for a year. Over 26 million working days were lost, the most since the 1926 General Strike.

items.title: Band Aid
items.line: 'Do They Know It's Christmas?' was recorded in one day at Sarm West in Notting Hill and released on 7 December 1984. It sold a million copies in its first week and stayed at number one for five weeks.

items.title: Spitting Image
items.line: Peter Fluck and Roger Law's latex puppets first went out on ITV on 26 February 1984, a 12-episode series mostly at 10pm. Clive Sinclair paid for the development.

items.title: Threads
items.line: The BBC's nuclear-war film, set in Sheffield and written by Barry Hines, aired on BBC2 on 23 September 1984. It cost £400,000 and drew 6.9 million viewers, the channel's best that week.

items.title: Torvill and Dean's Boléro
items.line: In Sarajevo the Nottingham pair skated to Ravel's Boléro for twelve perfect 6.0s and Olympic gold. More than 24 million people in Britain watched.

items.title: The Macintosh
items.line: Apple's Macintosh went on sale on 24 January 1984 at $2,495, two days after Ridley Scott's '1984' advert ran during the Super Bowl.

items.title: The Brighton hotel bombing
items.line: On 12 October 1984 an IRA bomb went off in the Grand Hotel during the Conservative conference. Five people were killed; Margaret Thatcher was unhurt.
